concepts.title: Development Communication: Meaning and Essential Features
concepts.definition: Development communication puts planned messaging to work as an engine of social and economic progress, chiefly for groups left behind. Its hallmarks: information flows both ways, people facing a problem are trusted to help solve it, mass media are blended with face-to-face channels, and content is shaped around who the audience is and where they live.
concepts.formula: two_way_dialogue plus audience_context plus motivation yields consensus and joint action
concepts.key_idea: Planned, two-way messaging that treats people as capable partners rather than passive receivers.
question_patterns: what is development communication and why is it called a catalyst for social change
who coined the term development communication and in which year
state four essential features of development communication
explain why development communication is described as a two way process
how does development communication build consensus between people and development agencies

solution_steps.explain: communication power used in a planned manner to advance an unequal society toward equity
orientation to socio-economic progress, community education, mixed media plus interpersonal channels, and audience-based design
information holders dialogue with the uninformed; motivation and consensus lead to concerted action

worked_examples.q: Planned messaging as an engine of social progress is called what communication: development or gossip?

concepts.title: Development Journalism and the Fourth Pillar
concepts.definition: A newer branch of reporting, born after colonial rule ended, that highlights how ordinary people adopt new techniques and improve community life instead of covering only struggles, disasters and wars. The press is counted as the fourth pillar that keeps democracy upright by carrying people's opinions and expression.
concepts.formula: development_journalism = success_stories plus people_at_work plus community_voices
concepts.key_idea: Reporting people's progress, not just conflicts, keeps democracy's fourth pillar strong.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe206.txt, Introduction and Basic Concepts (approx lines 117-171)
question_patterns: why is the press called the fourth pillar of democracy
distinguish development journalism from colonial era reporting
what does development journalism focus on today
explain the significance of development communication and journalism for an equitable society
how does journalism serve people's right to opinion and expression

solution_steps.explain: people's participation grounds democracy; media carry opinion and expression, so the press stands as the fourth pillar

solution_steps.action: contrast the old and new reporting
solution_steps.explain: pre-independence reporting followed colonial choices about struggles and disasters; today's development reporting describes people at work on new projects

worked_examples.q: The press is counted as which pillar of democracy: the fourth or the first?

concepts.title: Campaign as an Organised Communication Drive
concepts.definition: A time-bound, tightly organised drive that combines meetings, tours, newspaper articles, leaflets, exhibitions and drama around a single theme. Dramatic presentation across channels grabs attention, the message lodges in memory, and a climate for adopting new practices follows. Advocacy -- championing a cause such as preventing early marriage or deforestation through lobbying and alliances -- works in the same spirit.
concepts.formula: campaign_impact = attention plus interest plus memory plus action across many channels
concepts.key_idea: One theme, many channels, a fixed window -- intensity makes the message stick and moves people to act.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe206.txt, Method 1 Campaign and Swachh Bharat example (approx lines 272-286)
question_patterns: define a campaign and list the communication materials it combines
why does a campaign leave a lasting impression and stimulate action
describe the Swachh Bharat Mission as a nationwide campaign
what is advocacy and how does it support causes like preventing early marriage of girls
design a slogan for a campaign on any social issue of your choice

solution_steps.explain: an organised, intensive, fixed-period mix of meetings, tours, articles, leaflets and exhibitions on one theme
dramatics across channels earn attention and interest; memory and a conducive climate follow, ending in adoption of practices
advocacy backs a cause by lobbying governments and multilateral bodies, building alliances and informing supporters

worked_examples.q: A time-bound drive combining many channels around one theme is called a what: campaign or holiday?

concepts.title: Red Ribbon Express: Computing Campaign Reach
concepts.definition: Campaign reach can be measured. Aawareness trains such as the seven-coach Red Ribbon Express, run with NACO, NYKS, UNICEF and UNAIDS support, covered thousands of villages by halting at a fixed number of stations each year; dividing total village coverage by the halts gives the average villages served per stop.
concepts.key_idea: Coverage divided by halts gives the average villages served per stop.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe206.txt, Red Ribbon Express box (approx lines 230-269)
question_patterns: find the average number of villages the Red Ribbon Express served at each halt station
calculate villages covered per halt when annual village coverage and the number of halt stations are known
the awareness train covered 43,200 villages halting at 180 stations; how many villages does one halt reach on average
compute the per-station village coverage of a travelling exhibition campaign
how many villages were reached per halt station during the Red Ribbon Express journey across India

solution_steps.explain: spreading total villages evenly over the halt stations yields the average villages served per stop

worked_examples.q: How many coaches does the Red Ribbon Express carry: seven or seventy?

concepts.title: Radio, Community Radio and Television Outreach
concepts.definition: Radio is the cheapest, most portable mass medium, reaching listeners whom poor literacy shuts off from print. Community radio goes further: local people run the station, broadcast in their own dialect and turn the medium into their voice, while NGOs and educational institutions may seek licences. Television adds participatory formats and pairs education with entertainment, and the EDUSAT satellite, launched in September 2004, serves distance education exclusively.
concepts.formula: outreach = cheap_access plus local_voice plus interactive_formats
concepts.key_idea: Radio travels with the listener; community radio lets people speak in their own voice and dialect.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe206.txt, Method 2 Radio and Television (approx lines 295-366)
question_patterns: why is radio called the most accessible mass medium for development broadcasting
how is community radio different from All India Radio
list the programme formats in which radio development content is presented
name India's education satellite and state its purpose
how can television combine education with entertainment for common good

solution_steps.explain: low cost, mobility with the listener, and reach into low-literacy audiences beat print and suit development work
local people run and manage the station; content serves local use in the local dialect, letting communities voice problems
talk and reality shows invite participation; EDUSAT, launched 2004, was the first Indian satellite built only for education

worked_examples.q: Which is the cheapest, most portable mass medium: radio or television?

concepts.title: Print Media and Rural Development Reporting
concepts.definition: National and regional dailies lean urban, so agriculture and village problems stay low in priority, yet sustained press attention still works: the Project Village Chhatera column begun in 1969 reported one village's lives fortnightly and pulled machines, bridges, roads and banks into the area. Development journalists spend their day interviewing, attending press conferences and chasing story leads.
concepts.formula: press_effect = sustained_reporting plus services plus infrastructure brought to the area
concepts.key_idea: Steady rural reporting can haul services and infrastructure into neglected villages.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe206.txt, Method 3 Print media and Project Village Chhatera (approx lines 373-449)
question_patterns: why do rural development concerns get low priority in daily newspapers
describe the Project Village Chhatera experiment as a print media success story
how did regular press coverage transform village Chhatera
what working day tasks fill a development journalist's schedule
why is computer literacy essential for a print journalist working today

solution_steps.explain: bulk news is urban; reports on agriculture and village problems rank low, and rural periodicals are few
a fortnightly Hindustan Times column from 1969 wrote village stories with sensitivity and acted as a catalyst bringing services and benefits

worked_examples.q: Which village column begun in 1969 pulled services into one village: Project Village Chhatera or Page Three?

concepts.title: ICTs, Tele-centres and SEWA's Digital Push
concepts.definition: Information and Communication Technologies bundle computer hardware and software with digital broadcast and telecommunications. Mobile phones now carry banking, marketing, employment and public services, while tele-centre kiosks -- like the SARI project's 80 kiosks in Tamilnadu offering e-mail, browsing and e-government certificates -- deliver services directly. SEWA's Community Learning Centres train grassroots women in computers, radio, video and satellite tools for self-reliance.
concepts.formula: ict_power = mobile_services plus telecentre_kiosks plus grassroots_training
concepts.key_idea: Mobile networks and tele-centres turn information access into economic and social power for the poor.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe206.txt, Method 4 ICTs, SARI and SEWA examples (approx lines 409-472)
question_patterns: comment: ICTs are the future vehicles of development
what services did the SARI tele-centre kiosks offer in Tamilnadu
how did SEWA use ICTs to empower grassroots women workers
what is a tele-centre and how does it better the lives of the poor
list the technologies covered by the umbrella term ICT

solution_steps.explain: computer hardware and software plus digital broadcast and telecommunications together count as ICTs
kiosks offering computer education, e-mail, browsing and e-government reach the poor directly, as SARI showed
the women's union built Community Learning Centres for IT training, cutting time and cost of communication across districts

worked_examples.q: How many kiosks did the SARI project run in Tamilnadu: 80 or 8?

concepts.title: PSA Appraisal Scoring on the 0-3 Rubric
concepts.section: Practical 1: Study of Radio Public Service Announcement
concepts.definition: A recorded radio spot for public good can be judged with a ten-parameter rubric: message clarity, listener engagement, interest, awareness value, audience motivation, voice selection, sound recording clarity, sound effects, day-date-time suitability and mention of the source. Each parameter is rated 0 to 3, so the marks add up to a total out of 30.
concepts.key_idea: Ten rubric ratings on a 0-3 scale add to an appraisal score out of 30.
question_patterns: find the total score out of 30 when ten PSA rubric parameters are rated
add the ten parameter marks awarded to a recorded announcement
a group awards rubric ratings to a radio spot; calculate its appraisal score
how is the quality of a public service announcement scored on the 0-3 rubric
compute the appraisal total when five parameters score 2 and five score 3

solution_steps.explain: add the ratings for suitability, engagement, interest, awareness and motivation
solution_steps.compute: block_one = engage_score + interest_score + awareness_score + motivate_score + timing_score

solution_steps.explain: add the ratings for voice, message clarity, recording clarity, effects and source mention
solution_steps.compute: block_two = voice_score + message_score + sound_score + effect_score + source_score

solution_steps.explain: the ten parameter marks together give the score out of 30

worked_examples.q: The PSA rubric rates ten parameters on a 0 to what scale: 3 or 30?

concepts.title: PSA Duration Arithmetic
concepts.definition: A public service announcement is a brief jingle-style message broadcast between programmes, advertised for an idea rather than a product. Its planning length sits inside a permitted band -- classically 10 to 60 seconds -- so the typical duration is simply the midpoint of the allowed minimum and maximum.
concepts.key_idea: Typical spot length is the midpoint of the permitted minimum and maximum.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe206.txt, Public Service Announcement paragraph (approx lines 305-311)
question_patterns: find the midpoint duration of a public service message slotted between 10 and 60 seconds
a jingle slot allows 15 to 45 seconds; calculate its mean broadcast length
what is the average length of a spot permitted between 20 and 40 seconds
compute the typical duration of an announcement whose permitted band is 10 to 60 seconds
how long on average can a public service announcement run within its allowed band

solution_steps.explain: the shortest and longest permitted lengths bracket the typical spot, so their mean is the planned duration

worked_examples.q: PSAs classically run 10 to how many seconds: 60 or 6?

concepts.title: Skills and Career Avenues in Development Communication
concepts.section: Knowledge and Skills; Scope and Career avenues
concepts.definition: The professional needs cognitive grip to grasp issues, creative treatment to win attention, technical command of camera, video production and editing, plus presentation and interviewing technique, language command, Microsoft Office basics and laws of the field. Working with diverse groups and listening well matter as much; careers span print, TV, radio and community media, research, training, freelancing and consultancy.
concepts.formula: career_readiness = cognitive plus creative plus technical plus interpersonal plus language skills
concepts.key_idea: Media craft combined with social-work empathy opens careers across media houses, agencies, research and training.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe206.txt, Knowledge and Skills; Scope and Career avenues (approx lines 473-556)
question_patterns: what knowledge and skills does a career in development communication and journalism require
list four career avenues open to a development communication specialist
why must a development journalist question closely and travel to remote areas
explain the guiding principle of helping people help themselves in extension work
which technical skills prepare a student to work as a development filmmaker

solution_steps.explain: cognitive, creative, technical, presentation, questioning, interpersonal, language and computer skills with knowledge of media laws
development journalist, researcher, trainer of field functionaries, freelancer and consultant across government and non-government sectors

worked_examples.q: Which command covers camera, video production and editing: technical or financial?

worked_examples.question_pattern: A class group rates a recorded radio spot on the ten-parameter rubric: engagement {engage_score}, interest {interest_score}, awareness {awareness_score}, motivation {motivate_score}, day-time suitability {timing_score}, voice {voice_score}, message clarity {message_score}, recording clarity {sound_score}, effects {effect_score} and source mention {source_score}. Find the total score out of 30.

solution_template.compute: block_one = engage_score + interest_score + awareness_score + motivate_score + timing_score
block_two = voice_score + message_score + sound_score + effect_score + source_score

solution_template.explain: 13 + 13 = 26, so the spot scores 26 out of 30

worked_examples.question_pattern: An awareness train covered {villages_covered} villages in a year while halting at {halt_stations} stations. Compute the average number of villages served per halt.

solution_template.explain: 43200 / 180 = 240, so each halt served about 240 villages on average

worked_examples.question_pattern: A channel slots jingles between {slot_low} and {slot_high} seconds. What is the midpoint duration of such a public service message?
